transcript: One of my favorite parts about the wicked movie is how many times it pays homage to the original Broadway staging. So here are just a few of my favorites that I picked up during my first two watches of the film. And as a PSA, there will be spoilers for both the wicked movie and wicked musical in this video, so watch at your own peril. But let's start here, which is that the statue that they burn of Alphabet in the. The film is in the iconic defining gravity pose. And the way that they shoot it from an up angle really does give defining gravity vibes. During what is this feeling, we see a quick shot of Glinda and Elphaba sparring with poles, which reminded me a lot of the Broadway choreography when Glinda and Elphaba spar in Munchkinland. And I would not be surprised if that exact same choreography is called back in the second film. At the end of popular, we see Ariana Grande strike a very similar pose that Glinda strikes in the musical, with her looking up into a mirror. And speaking of popular, we actually got a couple of Easter eggs of popular choreography, not in the popular number, but in the Adina and Kristen cameos. During that scene, if you watch very closely, you can see Kristin Chenoweth with. Do her iconic leg flutter, and she also does a bit with her little torch that feels very reminiscent of her is This thing on bit that she did with her magic wand in popular. One of my favourite moments of the film is that in one short day we got reference to these guys with several of the dancers dressed in armless outfits that kind of resembled these. Now I believe this design is actually based on an illustration from the book, so it doubles as a reference to that, but I am counting it as a show reference anyway. I already made an entire video about how this opening shot is actually a reference to the original opening of the musical on Broadway. And we have this shot in Defying Gravity, which I know is not super subtle, but it is still crazy to me that they were able to make this work in a live action movie and still have it feel as epic as it did on stage. So like, mad props to John M. Chu on this one. I also really appreciate it that they gave a special thanks in the credits to the original creative team as well as the people who have worked on wicked throughout its 20+ year history. I thought this was a super classy touch.
